caption: Road works
colour: red triangle, black worker digging symbol
explanation: Warns that road works or a temporary obstruction lie ahead; slow down, watch for workers and changed road layout, and be ready to stop.
mnemonic: Man with a shovel means slow down.
notes: Commons description: 'Road works or temporary obstruction of the carriageway ahead.' Red warning triangle with black symbol of a worker digging. File confirmed via Commons file page.

caption: Loose chippings
colour: red triangle, car throwing up stones
explanation: Newly laid surface dressing means loose stone chippings on the road; slow right down to avoid skidding and protect your screen and paintwork from flying chips.
mnemonic: Loose stones, loose grip - ease off.
notes: Commons description: 'UK traffic sign: Loose chippings on road ahead (TSRGDNO 7009)'. Red warning triangle showing a car with stones thrown up from the wheels. File confirmed via Commons file page. Often paired with a '20 mph' advisory plate (7009.1).

caption: End of road works
explanation: Marks the end of the road works and of any temporary restrictions, including temporary speed limits; you may return to normal driving for the road.
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Highway Code caption: 'End of road works and any temporary restrictions including speed limits.' It is a plain white rectangle with black 'End' text (TSRGD diagram 2715 family); no single matching standalone SVG exists on Wikimedia Commons (2715/2716 are temporary-diversion junction signs, not this 'End' panel), so it is authored as a composite.

caption: Lane closed ahead
colour: lane diagram, red bar over closed lane
explanation: Shows which traffic lane is closed ahead, marked by a red bar; merge in good time into a lane that stays open and do not change lane at the last moment.
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Rectangular 'wicket' sign showing the carriageway lanes with a red bar over the lane that is closed (TSRGD 7202/7203 family). No standalone matching SVG exists on Wikimedia Commons (the 72-series index has no 7202/7203 file; 7404 is the rear-of-vehicle version), so authored as a composite.

caption: Temporary maximum speed ahead
colour: white circle, red ring, black number
explanation: Advises the maximum speed in mph that applies through the road works ahead; reduce speed now so you are within the limit before you reach the works.
mnemonic: Slow before the cones, not at them.
notes: Composite: drawn in-app. Advance warning of a temporary mandatory maximum speed at road works - a red-ring speed roundel (number varies, e.g. 40/50), often on a yellow backing board with 'works' wording. Because the number varies and it is the standard speed roundel rather than a fixed roadworks-specific SVG, it is authored as a composite. Highway Code caption: 'Maximum speed advised through road works.'

caption: Stop/Go board
explanation: A manually operated board controlling single-line traffic at road works; obey it exactly - wait at the STOP face and only move on when it is turned to GO.
mnemonic: Operator's board: STOP means stop, full stop.
notes: Commons description: 'United Kingdom traffic sign, used for manual traffic control, instructing vehicles to stop and wait. Sign no. 7024 is typically on the reverse of this sign.' STOP face is a red octagon with white 'STOP'; the reverse (diagram 7024) is a green circle with white 'GO'. File confirmed via Commons file page; asset depicts the STOP face.

caption: Slow-moving works traffic crossing
colour: red and white panel, works vehicle symbol
explanation: Warns of a slow-moving or stationary works vehicle operating on the carriageway ahead; be ready for it to cross or block a lane and pass only when safe in the direction shown.
mnemonic: Works vehicle = expect it to crawl.
notes: Commons description: 'UK traffic sign: Nature of work being done by vehicle working on the highway (TSRGDNO 7404)'. Used on/with slow-moving or stationary works vehicles working on the carriageway (pass in the direction indicated). Categories: 'Diagrams of road works road signs of the United Kingdom (7000)'. File confirmed via Commons file page.

caption: Diversion route
explanation: Marks a temporary diversion route around a closure or road works; follow the arrow and stay with the diversion symbol at each junction until it ends.
mnemonic: Follow the symbol all the way round.
notes: Commons description: 'UK traffic sign: Start of temporary diversion route to the right (TSRGDNO 2702)'. Black legend and directional arrow on yellow; continuation/'ends' variants are 2702L/2702V and symbolic routes use 2716. File confirmed via Commons file page.
